title: Context7 MCP Server
summary: Give your coding agent current library documentation and code examples through Upstash's Context7 MCP server, so it stops guessing at old APIs.
description: Context7 is an MCP server from Upstash that looks up documentation for a library at the version you use and hands the relevant snippets to the agent. It is aimed at the common failure where a model writes code against an API that has since changed.
This setup uses the hosted server over HTTP. It works without a key at a low rate limit, and an API key from the Context7 dashboard raises it.
useWhen: Use a framework that changed since your model was trained
Write code against a new library release
Look up the exact signature of a method before calling it
Stop the agent from inventing options that do not exist

mcp.name: context7

headers.name: Authorization
headers.description: Optional Context7 API key from the Context7 dashboard, for higher rate limits

access: Sends the library name and your question to the Context7 service
Returns documentation text; does not read your files

example.prompt: Using the current docs, show how to define a route handler in the latest Next.js and note anything that changed recently.
example.result: Pulled the App Router docs for your installed version: route handlers live in app/api/x/route.ts and export named functions per HTTP method. Example code included.

faq.question: Is a key required?
faq.answer: Not to start. The key is optional and lifts the rate limit. Create it in the Context7 dashboard.

faq.question: Does it see my code?
faq.answer: Only what the agent puts in the query, such as a library name and a question. It does not scan your project.

access: Sends queries to the Context7 hosted service
